newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - OCT 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - OCT 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--Government to issue long-term state bonds with fixed interest rates next year, in an effort to contain interest rates.

--1997 to be the year of talks on reform of the social security system, Prime Minister Costas Simitis tells Parliament during policy statement announcement last night. On the agenda is merging pension funds and social security bodies.
--Simitis fails to define the measures to ensure convergence. "Social dialogue" to ensure widest possible consensus to be pursued on all economic policies and budget.
--Credit Bank says it wants to increase competitiveness on a European level but that it does not intend to exchange block shares with Ergo Bank.
--Bank of Piraeus to get share capital increase of nine billion drachmas.
--Energy policies get a national focus. Development Minister Vasso Papandreou announces plans to turn Greece into transport and energy hub for Balkan, Black Sea countries towards the West.
IMERISIA

--Simitis announces four years of bold decision-taking to develop the Greek economy and to participate by year 2000 at the latest, in economic and monetary union (EMU). The central and standing aim of the government, he says, is equal participation in EMU.

--Public works get the green light. Some 7000 projects "set to change the face of Greece" to receive 4.3 trillion drachmas and will form the foundation stones for growth in the next four years. Private participation in projects to be bolstered.

--Wage increases above inflation for public servants. Fiscal adjustment, Simitis says, cannot be achieved on the basis of wage restrictions. Incomes policy will keep the peace between stabilisation and social cohesion.
--Dialogue on reform of social security sector to begin next year. Talks will be based on the principle that social insurance is obligatory and guaranteed by the state.
KERDOS
--Government's programme of good intentions, markets say. But Simitis fails to commit himself to specific choices, measures or policies.
--Government forecasts Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth at over 3.0 percent for 1997 and aims at a growth rate of 5.0 percent by 1999.
--Twelve state utilities and organisations (DEKO) ready to seek managers/consultants from private sector. Economy ministry gives remaining 23 DEKOs till the end of November to change guidelines.
EXPRESS

--The goal is the creation of a competitive economy, Simitis says. The logic of 'political cost' put aside while the government works towards getting the economy ready for EMU by the end of the decade.
--Markets react positively to policy statements but await more details. The 1997 budget will show whether word and deed are one.
--Fiscal policies: Simitis makes no reference to new taxes but stresses abolition of tax breaks, fight against tax evasion and reform of finance ministry services.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Clear goals with unclear means of achieving them. Policy statements balance stabilisation and social cohesion but Simitis gives no indication as to how he will achieve his goals. --Positive messages from retail sales indices.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
